title: Cluster 02 DRILL: Microevolution and the Hardy-Weinberg Model
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 7 · 8 questions · 84 marks · 26 parts · one mark per minute, so about an hour and a half · every question but one is an actual exam paper question
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE; a right answer said confidently moves on.

Every question here is a real exam paper question except one. Question 7(e) is constructed, and its answer says so in its first line. Everything else is the paper's own wording, and where a stem has been edited it is only so that it stands without the parts of the original that came before it, with the edit written out in the Sources block.

Eight questions, 84 marks, 26 parts. This cluster owns five of Core Idea 4's fourteen outcomes, 4(d), 4(e), 4(f), 4(m) and 4(n). Two of those five are Hardy-Weinberg.

Read the box above Question 7 before you start it. Hardy-Weinberg is the one topic in the whole course where the syllabus tests more than the papers does. The syllabus prints p² + 2pq + q² = 1 in its Mathematical Requirements alongside the t-test and chi-squared, and 9477 Specimen P1 Q25 put it on the paper, but the entire 1650-question bank holds five records that mention it, because the papers are 9744-era. Question 7 uses four of those five and constructs the fifth part to reach the coverage the outcome demands.

Drift against selection is the discrimination this cluster is built around. Q1(c), Q2(b), Q2(c), Q3(a), Q3(b) and Q3(c) all ask you to decide whether a change in allele frequency was caused by selection or by chance, and the schemes reject the wrong one by name. Getting this right is worth more here than any definition.

Two real figures. Both are the real image from the paper the question came from, not a redrawing.

Two MCQs, both real, both audited. Q6(a) is 9477 Specimen Paper 1 Question 25, the only Hardy-Weinberg question on the entire official specimen. Q7(d) is a real prelim MCQ that makes you do the 2pq arithmetic, apply the founder effect and name an isolating mechanism inside one row.

Cumulative over Books 2, 3 and 6. Every Hardy-Weinberg part needs allele, genotype, homozygous, heterozygous, dominant and recessive used exactly. Q4(a) and Q7 need you to read a genotype off a phenotype, which only works for the homozygous recessive. Q3(b) and Q8 need mutation as the source of new alleles.

What the marks reward. Write the population is the smallest unit that can evolve, never that an individual evolved. Say that drift is random and that selection is not. For a bottleneck, say the survivors are a random sample, that diversity is lost, and that the loss persists after recovery. In every calculation, enter through q².

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required answers as well as duplicated labels. Q1 what the unit of evolution is, and using an adaptive prediction to rule selection out · Q2 the same species, two populations, one explained by drift and one by selection · Q3 drift and selection compared, then separated inside three rival theories · Q4 seven short Suggests on seven organisms the notes never mention · Q5 the three mechanisms that preserve variation, at essay length · Q6 what a model predicts, then a fitness table that has to be answered with its own figures · Q7 the whole of Hardy-Weinberg, four real questions and one constructed · Q8 chance and isolation held together in one answer. Declared overlaps, and there are two. Heterozygote advantage is argued as a mechanism in Q5 and quantified as fitness values in Q6(b); the schemes score different things and Q6(b) rejects the bare phrase. Independent assortment and random fertilisation appear in Q8 as chance events and in Cluster 1 Q1(b) as sources of variation.

Nothing from Cluster 3, and nothing from Books 8 or 9. The biological species concept, the four-stage speciation model, prezygotic against postzygotic barriers, phylogenetic trees, classification and multiple sequence alignment are Cluster 3. Q7(d) and Q8 name isolating mechanisms only because their own mark schemes do; neither asks you to define one.
